newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair goes green with gas-driven car.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair goes green with gas-driven car.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair bolstered his green credentials on Wednesday with the news he is converting his family car to run on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
Environment minister Michael Meacher, speaking at the launch in south London of a fleet of natural gas vehicles, told reporters Blair had ordered the conversion of his Ford Galaxy.
Vehicles running on LPG and natural gas are widely recognised as cleaner and quieter than conventional petrol driven engines.
While Blair's personal choice will find support from green lobbyists his government is under criticism for not doing enough to promote pollution free transport.
The previous Conservative government reduced excise duties on road fuel gases but finance minister Gordon Brown left them unchanged in his July budget.
Environmentalists and the gas industry want the excise duty erased altogether encouraging more road users to make the investment in switching their cars to gas.
Tax breaks have put hundreds of thousands of LPG vehicles on the road elsewhere in Europe where Holland, Italy and France lead the way.
Britain's first purpose-built LPG bus was launched in June. Cars can be converted to run on both LPG and petrol at a cost of about a thousand pounds.
